title: Area of Rectangles and Composite Figures
seo_title: Grade 3 Area Worksheets: Rectangles and Composite Figures (TEKS 3.6C, 3.6D, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.6C determine the area of rectangles with whole number side lengths in problems using multiplication related to the number of rows times the number of unit squares in each row; 3.6D decompose composite figures formed by rectangles into non-overlapping rectangles to determine the area of the original figure using the additive property of area
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 area worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.6C and 3.6D: rows times squares, count square units, rectangles with side lengths, composite figures split into rectangles and word problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Area of a rectangle = rows × squares in each row.
key_sub: Split a composite figure into rectangles that do not overlap, then add their areas.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Area is the number of unit squares that cover a shape, with no gaps or overlaps.
  • A rectangle is rows of squares: area = number of rows × squares in each row = length × width.
  • Area uses square units: square inches, square feet, square centimeters.
  • For a composite figure, cut it into rectangles that do not overlap, find each area, and add.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the sides (that is perimeter)Area multiplies: rows × squares in each row.
Writing ft instead of square feetArea is always in square units.
Multiplying the outside lengths of an L-shapeCut it into rectangles first, then add their areas.

faq.a: Find the area of rectangles with whole-number side lengths by multiplying the number of rows by the number of unit squares in each row.
Split composite figures made of rectangles into non-overlapping rectangles and add their areas to find the area of the whole figure.

faq.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
faq.a: Area is the space inside, in square units. Perimeter is the distance around, in units.

faq.q: How do you find a missing side if you know the area?
faq.a: Divide the area by the side you know. A 24 square inch rectangle with a 6 inch side has a 4 inch side.
